member.summary:
Builds and caches "x-ray" copies of entity/paperdoll textures where each pixel's ALPHA is remapped by TWO factors, both aimed at making the character read as BEHIND cover rather than pasted on top: 1. BRIGHTNESS — darker pixels stay more opaque (dark gear/hair stay visible; a dark hair staying opaque is exactly what keeps the bald scalp from showing through it), while bright pixels (skin, light cloth) go see-through so the cover shows through them. 2. VERTICAL POSITION — the LOWER part of the body becomes more transparent than the upper part (a smooth bottom-to-top gradient within each sprite cell). This mimics being occluded from below: your legs/feet hide behind the trunk/wall while your head peeks out — a strong "I'm behind something" depth cue.
Same approach as : the remap is a per-pixel CPU pass done once per source texture and cached, so the hot draw path swaps in the prebuilt texture. The source pixel's own alpha (feathered edges, transparency) is preserved as a multiplier so edges stay smooth and fully-transparent pixels stay fully transparent.

member.name: M:Intersect.Client.Entities.Player.TrySettleSubTileToTileCenter
member.summary:
FINISH-THE-STEP (tile-to-tile combat alignment, final design 2026-07-17): sub-tile movement lets the player STOP between tile centres, but every combat rule (adjacency, cardinal facing, mob chase) speaks whole tiles — a fractional resting position makes melee look like it connects across a visible gap. When movement input goes idle off-centre, the character keeps walking FORWARD — the direction already being walked — until the next tile centre: the standard grid-game "commit to the tile transition" rule (facing unchanged, walk cycle just continues, a released tap completes a clean tile).
THE THREE HARD RULES, each one bought with a failed playtest — do not relax them: 1. FORWARD ONLY. Never a backward or sideways correction step: any motion that isn't a continuation of the player's own walk reads as "the game moved me" (backward scoots and perpendicular slides both failed playtest). 2. ONE-SHOT. If the forward step is blocked (wall, or the mob itself on the next tile), GIVE UP where we stand (`_settleSuspendedUntilNextInput`) — resting a quarter-tile off is fine; combat gates open and behave exactly as before this system existed. 3. CANCEL ON SERVER CORRECTION. An `EntityPositionPacket` for the local player calls — the server disagreed (usually a mob contesting the tile), and retrying is how the endless client/server snap loop happened: client-initiated automatic movement ALWAYS loses races against moving entities, because a human stops pressing but automatic retries don't. Only real player input re-arms the system.
Steps go through the normal validated per-step move path (), so zero server/packet changes. Guards mirror ProcessDirectionalInput's: no finishing while casting (a move would cancel the cast), during click-move (it owns movement and already ends on tile centres), mid-step, dead, or in dialogs.

member.name: M:Intersect.Client.Entities.Player.SuspendAutoSettleUntilNextInput
member.summary: Rule 3 of the finish-the-step system: the server sent this client a position correction (EntityPositionPacket), meaning our view of the world disagreed with authority — typically a mob moving into the tile a finish step was entering. Automatic movement must NEVER retry after that (endless correction loop, playtest 2026-07-17); only real player input re-arms it.

member.summary:
Client-side auto-loot, scoped to the player's own kill drops. A ground item is only eligible when the server stamped it Owner == me — that is exactly how NPC kills mark their loot. Items another player drops by hand (owner empty), loot locked to someone else, and free-for-all drops never trigger it.
Flow: the character walks itself to the nearest owned drop, picks the first item from pickup range, and the remaining owned drops inside the pickup radius then cascade in — one send per tick, so the icons pop and fly to the character staggered instead of all at once.
